WMT.rationale: Walmart is a fundamentally healthy, dominant retailer with strong competitive positioning (world's largest retailer, ~8.6% U.S. retail market share, 26% grocery share, wide moat per Morningstar). YoY growth in the latest quarter (Q1 FY2027) was solid: revenue +7.3%, EPS +19.6%, net income +18.3%. E-commerce is growing 24% YoY and advertising business grew 46%, providing higher-margin growth vectors. However, several factors temper enthusiasm. QoQ trends show deceleration: revenue -1.0%, EPS -13.0%, operating cash flow -47.9%. The TTM data is incomplete due to fiscal calendar gaps, limiting full-year assessment. Valuation has compressed from a peak P/E of ~53x in late April 2026 to ~38.7x currently, but this still represents a significant premium to the retail industry average (~18.5x) and peers (~24.6x). A DCF model from Simply Wall St suggests fair value around $98.74, well below the current $111.84 price. Near-term headwinds are real: Cleveland Research flagged slowing U.S. comparable store sales (July 1 news), the stock fell 4.5% on that report, and management is using tariff refunds to offset aggressive inventory clearance pricing. Fuel costs absorbed ~$175M of operating income per the earnings call. The stock is down ~10.3% over the last quarter. On the positive side, the P/E has pulled back to the low end of its 365-day range (37.6-55.4), and consensus EPS estimates for FY2027 point to +9.4% growth with Q2 EPS expected at $0.74 (+8.3% YoY). The next earnings date (Aug 20, 2026) could serve as a catalyst if results beat expectations. Net: solid franchise with durable competitive advantages, but valuation remains elevated for a low-margin retailer, and near-term same-store sales deceleration creates risk. Mildly attractive at current levels after the pullback, but not compelling enough for a stronger score.
